gloss: to be photographed, to appear (in a photo)

definitions.gloss: to be photographed, to come out (in a photo)
definitions.explanation: For a person or thing to appear in a photograph or image. Describes how well or clearly the subject is captured.

definitions.gloss: to be copied, to be reproduced
definitions.explanation: For something to be transcribed or reproduced onto paper or another surface.

examples.japanese: {写真|しゃしん}にきれいに{写|うつ}った。
examples.english: It came out nicely in the photo.

examples.japanese: {暗|くら}くて{顔|かお}がよく{写|うつ}っていない。
examples.english: It was dark and the face didn't come out well.

examples.japanese: {背景|はいけい}に{富士山|ふじさん}が{写|うつ}っている。
examples.english: Mt. Fuji appears in the background.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}いコピー{機|き}なので、{文字|もじ}がきれいに{写|うつ}らない。
examples.english: The copier is old, so the text doesn't come out clearly.

examples.japanese: {集合写真|しゅうごうしゃしん}で{全員|ぜんいん}がちゃんと{写|うつ}っているか{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked whether everyone came out properly in the group photo.

examples.japanese: カーボン{紙|し}を{使|つか}うと、{下|した}の{紙|かみ}にも{写|うつ}る。
examples.english: If you use carbon paper, it copies onto the sheet underneath.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pair: {写|うつ}す (transitive, to copy/photograph).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{写真|しゃしん}に{写|うつ}る (appear in a photo)
・きれいに{写|うつ}る (come out nicely)
・よく{写|うつ}る (come out well)
・{写|うつ}っている (is shown/captured in)

HOMOPHONES:
・{写|うつ}る: to be photographed, to be copied
・{映|うつ}る: to be reflected, to be projected on screen
・{移|うつ}る: to move, to transfer

{写|うつ}る focuses on photographic and copy reproduction, while {映|うつ}る is about reflections and on-screen images.
